items.title: RBI approves amalgamation of Indian branches of Emirates NBD Bank P.J.S.C. with RBL Bank Limited
items.summary: The Reserve Bank of India has sanctioned the Scheme of Amalgamation of Indian branches of Emirates NBD Bank P.J.S.C. (Transferor Bank) with RBL Bank Limited (Transferee Bank). The Scheme has been sanctioned in exercise of the powers contained in sub-section (4) of Section 44A of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949. The effective date of the amalgamation shall be December 01, 2026. All the Indian branches of Emirates NBD Bank P.J.S.C. will function as branches of RBL Bank Limited with effect from December 01, 2026. (Brij Raj) Chief General Manager Press Release: 2026-2027/1342

items.title: NATCO Pharma subsidiary launches Carboplatin in US market to address shortages

Despite having a higher profitability compared to peers, IDBI Bank's gross non-performing asset ratio remains concerning. The bank's success will rely on its ability to enhance asset quality while maintaining earnings growth.

items.title: Correcting rupee against fundamentals ultimately futile, says RBI's ex-guv Subbarao
items.summary: D Subbarao advocates for allowing the rupee to find its level based on economic fundamentals. He criticizes costly short-term measures that do not address structural issues behind capital outflows. The rupee's recent recovery followed the Reserve Bank of India's measures to reduce dollar demand. Subbarao highlights the importance of tax reforms to attract foreign investment in India.

items.title: Reality shows, cricket turn advertisers' safe bets
items.summary: Established non-fiction shows such as Bigg Boss and Kaun Banega Crorepati have continued to attract advertisers despite the blackout. Bigg Boss has roped in 95 sponsors across its language editions, while KBC has secured 25 sponsors. Cricket is also drawing advertiser interest, with India matches providing an opportunity to reach large audiences in a second half of the year largely devoid of marquee events such as the IPL or ICC tournaments. The India-West Indies series has drawn a strong response from brands, while the India-New Zealand series is also expected to see strong traction.

items.title: PM-KUSUM 2.0 may be aligned with farm schemes: Renewable energy secretary Santosh Kumar Sarangi
items.summary: The government plans to expand PM KUSUM to include incentives for modern irrigation practices among farmers. This expansion will encourage the use of solar-powered water pumps and promote remunerative crops. The ministries of renewable energy and agriculture are collaborating to align this initiative with existing schemes. New components such as agrivoltaics will also be integrated in the next phase.

items.title: Private banks' margins fall as FCNR deposits raise funding costs
items.summary: In the second quarter, leading private sector banks in India reported a drop in net interest margins. This decline was primarily caused by the costs associated with foreign currency non-resident deposits. Analysts noted that the leveraged nature of these deposits significantly impacted profitability. Additionally, banks faced pressure from faster repricing of assets as interest rates declined.

items.title: Exporters may be asked to monitor supply chains' indirect emissions
items.summary: The Indian government is engaging in discussions about measuring Scope 3 emissions for exporters. This consideration arises as trade partners impose tighter green requirements globally. Current frameworks focus on direct emissions and exclude indirect ones, making compliance more complex. As a result, industries, especially MSMEs, may face compliance burdens if new requirements are implemented. Ultimately, the aim is to ensure that Indian exporters remain competitive in international markets.

items.title: Farmers face 15% loss as poultry feed costs surge
items.summary: Poultry farmers are currently experiencing losses of approximately 15% due to rising livestock feed costs. Key ingredients have seen price increases of up to 75%, affecting farmers' ability to cope. Dairy producers, particularly in drought-affected regions, struggle to source necessary fodder for their livestock. Feed manufacturers are also feeling the impact as higher prices reduce demand for their products.

items.title: Banks also count cost of insurance payout curbs
items.summary: Central Bank of India anticipates a 33% decline in bancassurance fees due to proposed regulations. Canara Bank expects a ₹145-crore hit to its fee income from similar changes. Axis Bank aims to mitigate losses through increased sales volumes and alternative income sources. HDFC Bank has not yet assessed the potential impact of the new rules.

items.title: South film producers in thrall to streaming deals
items.summary: Jailer 2, a film starring Rajinikanth, has not been released in major Hindi theaters due to a disagreement. The producer declined to extend the theatrical window from four weeks to eight weeks. Southern films are increasingly prioritizing streaming rights over traditional box-office success, impacting overall profitability. Analysts believe that longer theatrical runs benefit producers and the film ecosystem as a whole.

items.title: Anup Bagchi backs 'exceptional' team as he connects the dots at HDFC Bank
items.summary: Anup Bagchi is set to take charge as MD and CEO of HDFC Bank starting October 27. He is currently familiarizing himself with the bank's balance sheet and profitability structure. Bagchi aims to engage with regulators, customers, and stakeholders to gather insights before implementing changes. His focus is on understanding the organization's operations rather than rushing into strategic alterations.

items.title: Defence canteens suspend orders for 3 Old Monk variants after Maharashtra FSSAI action
items.summary: Orders for three variants of Old Monk rum have been suspended by the defence ministry's canteen stores department due to regulatory action taken by the FSSAI in Maharashtra. This suspension, which affects sales across CSD's network, follows concerns over product labeling and deceptive marketing practices related to these alcoholic beverages.

items.title: Haier India to invest ₹7,000 crore in new facility in Andhra
items.summary: Haier India plans a ₹7,000 crore investment in a manufacturing facility in Andhra Pradesh, marking its largest investment in the country. The facility, expected to create 21,000 jobs by 2032, will focus on producing various home appliances and is strategically located in the rapidly growing Tirupati-Chennai-Nellore electronics corridor.

items.title: Uniqlo India net profit rises 41% to Rs 253 cr in FY26; co bets on expansion
items.summary: Uniqlo reported a significant increase in revenue for the year ended March 2026. The revenue rose 44% year-on-year, reaching ₹1,724 crore as net profit also increased. This growth occurred despite challenges faced by other apparel retailers in India. Uniqlo plans to expand its presence through new stores and enhance customer engagement via digital platforms. The Indian apparel market is projected to grow significantly in the coming years.

items.title: Eateries cut corners as high costs and hygiene crackdowns take a toll
items.summary: Amid rising food inflation, many Indian restaurants are implementing various strategies to manage costs. These strategies include pausing high-cost menu items and introducing smaller portions for diners. Increased operational expenses due to regulatory compliance have also led to price hikes for consumers. Many restaurant operators indicate they must share some inflation costs with patrons to maintain profitability. Consequently, price increases of 10-15% are expected across several restaurants in Mumbai.

items.title: 'Govt has no plans to regulate airfares'
items.summary: India's government has clarified that it will not regulate ticket prices for airlines under new rules. The new air fare regulations will allow the government to set limits during extraordinary situations like natural calamities. Airlines will need to get their fares approved by the Directorate General of Civil Aviation a month in advance. Recent data indicates that average airfares this festive season have increased significantly due to higher fuel costs.

items.title: Who is Amal Kelshikar? Why did he resign from the position of Torrent Pharmaceuticals' Executive Director? Explained

The company aims to increase its current portfolio of 2 GW to 7 GW by the year 2030. Engie will focus on renewable projects, battery storage, and data centre opportunities to achieve this goal. Challenges such as grid connectivity and land access will require innovative solutions, which the company is prepared to tackle.

items.title: Ahmedabad to become a key Vande Bharat maintenance centre: Rs 307 crore hub to handle everything from coach repairs to traction motors
items.summary: Ahmedabad is set to get a Rs 307 crore Vande Bharat train maintenance hub at Sabarmati, enabling major repairs and scheduled overhauls to be carried out locally. Being developed under Phase II of the Sabarmati Integrated Coaching Depot, the facility will handle heavy repairs, wheel and axle maintenance, and electrical equipment overhauls. It is designed to service 24-coach trainsets, with an annual capacity of 12 trainsets for SS-I maintenance or eight for SS-II maintenance.

items.title: Meta revises terms governing website content: What's new and changed? What rights do publishers retain now? Explained

items.title: India vs China in 40 years: TRUST MF CIO Mihir Vora - 'India compounded GDP growth at 7.3%; China broke out at 11.3%'

The company launched its first luxury housing project in Gurugram, resulting in high demand and strong sales. During the first half of the fiscal year, total income rose to Rs 3,098.06 crore compared to the previous year. Its consolidated net profit showed a slight increase, reaching Rs 761.

items.title: Faster services imports threaten to erode cushion against India’s goods trade deficit: Report
items.summary: India's services trade surplus has declined as imports grew faster than exports, leading to concerns about foreign exchange earnings. In September 2026, net services exports fell by 10 percent to USD 16.9 billion. Despite strong growth in merchandise exports of 23 percent, the services sector faces challenges. While cumulative net services exports increased during the first half, their sustainability is uncertain.

His meetings will take place in Mumbai and Jamnagar, focusing on investment and energy. The two countries have faced considerable delays in finalizing a trade agreement due to several ongoing challenges.

India’s soybean output seen falling 2.1% to 107.93 lakh tonnes in Kharif 2026: Farmers' body
items.summary: India's soybean production forecast indicates a slight decline to 107.93 lakh tonnes during the ongoing Kharif season. Drought-like conditions in Maharashtra, Karnataka, and Telangana are contributing to this reduction in output. However, increased production in Madhya Pradesh and Rajasthan is expected to compensate for these losses. The area cultivated with soybean increased by approximately 5 lakh hectares compared to the previous season.

items.title: 'India an important ally': Rubio says Trump weighing impact of Russia-related tariffs
items.summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio stated that India's energy requirements will be considered before possible sanctions on Russian oil. President Donald Trump recently waived certain provisions of a proposed sanctions law affecting major importers of Russian crude. Rubio emphasized the need for time to assess the impact of these measures on global economies. He highlighted the strategic partnership with India as an important factor in decision-making.

items.title: Christmas cheer, but caution remains: Exporters welcome US tariff relief, keep diversification plans
items.summary: US President Donald Trump’s decision to waive proposed tariffs of up to 100% on buyers of Russian oil has eased uncertainty for Indian exporters ahead of the crucial Christmas shipping season. However, businesses across textiles, gems and jewellery, and human hair products say they will continue diversifying export markets after last year’s tariff turmoil, even as the US remains a key destination for Indian goods.

items.title: India notifies first tariff cuts under New Zealand FTA
items.summary: India will implement duty concessions for certain imports from New Zealand starting October 20, under a new FTA. The concessions include zero basic customs duty for sheep meat and specific rates for fish and wine. Additionally, provisions have been made for manuka honey and kiwi fruit imports with varying duties. Sensitive categories like dairy products are excluded from this trade liberalization agreement.

items.title: Commerce Ministry organizes “Leveraging FTAs” outreach program in Jaipur to boost exports
items.summary: The Commerce Ministry organized an outreach event in Jaipur, targeting exporters to clarify the use of benefits provided by India's free trade agreements. This initiative aims to translate preferential market access into tangible export opportunities for Indian enterprises, emphasizing Rajasthan's strengths in textiles, handicrafts, and gems. Plans for coordination among stakeholders are outlined to optimize support for exporters moving forward.

items.title: Rs 3,600 crore business enquiries at 5-day handicraft fair
items.summary: Over 7,300 buyers participated in the 62nd IHGF Delhi Fair held from October 13 to 17. Business enquiries at the fair totaled Rs 3,600 crore, demonstrating strong international interest. Buyers from 105 countries, including the US, UK, and Germany, were present. Many brands indicated a significant shift toward sourcing more products from Indian manufacturers. India's handicraft exports reached $3.75 billion for the fiscal year 2025-26.

items.title: US' Russia sanction waiver a relief for India's exporters, energy security: Experts
items.summary: The waiver of sanctions under the Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act provides relief for India's energy security. Experts believe that continued access to Russian crude will support economic growth and ease inflationary pressures. While the waiver offers temporary relief, uncertainty remains regarding future contracts and investments. Trade organizations express hope for improving bilateral trade relations and advancing discussions between India and the US.

items.title: Who will pay for today's optimism if AI goes wrong? CEA Anantha Nageswaran answers
items.summary: Chief Economic Adviser Anantha Nageswaran raised concerns over the financial risks linked to artificial intelligence. He stated that finance ministries, central banks, and households could face costs from misplaced optimism. Even if AI expectations are met, these entities may still incur expenses. Nageswaran intends to outline five specific risks regarding this issue. He plans to suggest potential government actions to mitigate these risks in future discussions.
